claim: The large intracellular C-terminus of the P2X7 ion channel receptor is associated with diverse P2X7R-specific functions.
source: The large intracellular C-terminus of the pro-inflammatory P2X7 ion channel receptor (P2X7R) is associated with diverse P2X7R-specific functions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about P2X7R structure-function relationships.

claim: Cryo-EM structures of the closed and ATP-bound open full-length P2X7R identified a membrane-associated anchoring domain.
source: Cryo-EM structures of the closed and ATP-bound open full-length P2X7R recently identified a membrane-associated anchoring domain, an open-state stabilizing "cap" domain, and a globular "ballast domain" containing GTP/GDP and dinuclear Zn2+-binding sites with unknown functions.
evidence: This refers to recently published cryo-EM structural data.

claim: Cryo-EM structures of the closed and ATP-bound open full-length P2X7R identified an open-state stabilizing cap domain.
source: Cryo-EM structures of the closed and ATP-bound open full-length P2X7R recently identified a membrane-associated anchoring domain, an open-state stabilizing "cap" domain, and a globular "ballast domain" containing GTP/GDP and dinuclear Zn2+-binding sites with unknown functions.
evidence: This refers to recently published cryo-EM structural data.

claim: Cryo-EM structures of the closed and ATP-bound open full-length P2X7R identified a globular ballast domain containing GTP/GDP and dinuclear Zn2+-binding sites with unknown functions.
source: Cryo-EM structures of the closed and ATP-bound open full-length P2X7R recently identified a membrane-associated anchoring domain, an open-state stabilizing "cap" domain, and a globular "ballast domain" containing GTP/GDP and dinuclear Zn2+-binding sites with unknown functions.
evidence: This refers to recently published cryo-EM structural data.

claim: The authors improved incorporation of ANAP into Xenopus laevis oocyte-expressed P2X7Rs.
source: To investigate protein dynamics during channel activation, we improved incorporation of the environment-sensitive fluorescent unnatural amino acid L-3-(6-acetylnaphthalen-2-ylamino)–2-aminopropanoic acid (ANAP) into Xenopus laevis oocyte-expressed P2X7Rs and performed voltage clamp fluorometry.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study described in the abstract.

claim: The authors confirmed predicted conformational changes within the extracellular domain of P2X7R.
source: While we confirmed predicted conformational changes within the extracellular and the transmembrane domains, only 3 out of 41 mutants containing ANAP in the C-terminal domain resulted in ATP-induced fluorescence changes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the VCF experiments described in the abstract.

claim: The authors confirmed predicted conformational changes within the transmembrane domains of P2X7R.
source: While we confirmed predicted conformational changes within the extracellular and the transmembrane domains, only 3 out of 41 mutants containing ANAP in the C-terminal domain resulted in ATP-induced fluorescence changes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the VCF experiments described in the abstract.

claim: Only 3 out of 41 mutants containing ANAP in the C-terminal domain resulted in ATP-induced fluorescence changes.
source: While we confirmed predicted conformational changes within the extracellular and the transmembrane domains, only 3 out of 41 mutants containing ANAP in the C-terminal domain resulted in ATP-induced fluorescence changes.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the VCF experiments described in the abstract.

claim: The ballast domain functions rather independently from the extracellular ATP binding domain.
source: We conclude that the ballast domain functions rather independently from the extracellular ATP binding domain and might require activation by additional ligands and/or protein interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the limited fluorescence changes observed in the C-terminal domain.

claim: The ballast domain might require activation by additional ligands and/or protein interactions.
source: We conclude that the ballast domain functions rather independently from the extracellular ATP binding domain and might require activation by additional ligands and/or protein interactions.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observed lack of ATP-induced conformational changes in the ballast domain.

claim: P2X receptors are trimeric non-selective cation channels that are activated by extracellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
source: P2X receptors (P2XR) are trimeric non-selective cation channels that are activated by extracellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
evidence: This is established knowledge about P2X receptors cited in the introduction.

claim: The structure of a single P2X subunit has been compared to a dolphin.
source: The structure of a single P2X subunit has been compared to a dolphin, with two transmembrane domains (TM1 and TM2) that form the 'fluke', and a large extracellular domain, comprising the 'body', left and right 'flippers', and a 'head' domain that reaches over one of three inter-subunit ATP binding sites (Kawate et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a description from previous structural studies cited in the introduction.

claim: The intracellular N- and C-termini are short in most P2X subtypes.
source: The intracellular N- and C-termini are short in most P2X subtypes and have only been resolved in the open state of the P2X3R and, more recently, in the open and closed states of the P2X7R (Mansoor et al., 2016; McCarthy et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about P2X receptor structure cited in the introduction.

claim: The intracellular termini have only been resolved in the open state of the P2X3R and in the open and closed states of the P2X7R.
source: The intracellular N- and C-termini are short in most P2X subtypes and have only been resolved in the open state of the P2X3R and, more recently, in the open and closed states of the P2X7R (Mansoor et al., 2016; McCarthy et al., 2019).
evidence: This refers to specific structural studies cited in the introduction.

claim: The pro-inflammatory P2X7 subtype is expressed in immune cells and considered an important drug target.
source: The pro-inflammatory P2X7 subtype is expressed in immune cells and considered an important drug target.
evidence: This is established knowledge about P2X7 cited in the introduction.

claim: P2X7 has a low ATP sensitivity compared to other P2XR family members.
source: In contrast to the other P2XR family members, it has a low ATP sensitivity, shows complete lack of desensitization, and contains a large intracellular C-terminus (240 amino acids [aa]), which mediates diverse downstream effects such as interleukin secretion, plasma membrane permeabilization, blebbing, phosphatidylserine flip, and cell death (Kopp et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about P2X7 properties cited in the introduction.

claim: P2X7 shows complete lack of desensitization.
source: In contrast to the other P2XR family members, it has a low ATP sensitivity, shows complete lack of desensitization, and contains a large intracellular C-terminus (240 amino acids [aa]), which mediates diverse downstream effects such as interleukin secretion, plasma membrane permeabilization, blebbing, phosphatidylserine flip, and cell death (Kopp et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about P2X7 properties cited in the introduction.

claim: P2X7 contains a large intracellular C-terminus of 240 amino acids.
source: In contrast to the other P2XR family members, it has a low ATP sensitivity, shows complete lack of desensitization, and contains a large intracellular C-terminus (240 amino acids [aa]), which mediates diverse downstream effects such as interleukin secretion, plasma membrane permeabilization, blebbing, phosphatidylserine flip, and cell death (Kopp et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about P2X7 structure cited in the introduction.

claim: The P2X7 C-terminus mediates diverse downstream effects such as interleukin secretion, plasma membrane permeabilization, blebbing, phosphatidylserine flip, and cell death.
source: In contrast to the other P2XR family members, it has a low ATP sensitivity, shows complete lack of desensitization, and contains a large intracellular C-terminus (240 amino acids [aa]), which mediates diverse downstream effects such as interleukin secretion, plasma membrane permeabilization, blebbing, phosphatidylserine flip, and cell death (Kopp et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about P2X7 function cited in the introduction.

claim: Intertwined β-strands from all three subunits form an open state-stabilizing cap domain in P2X7R.
source: Accordingly, intertwined β-strands from all three subunits form an open state-stabilizing 'cap domain', that was also found in the P2X3R (Mansoor et al., 2016).
evidence: This refers to structural features identified in cryo-EM studies.

claim: The cap domain was also found in the P2X3R.
source: Accordingly, intertwined β-strands from all three subunits form an open state-stabilizing 'cap domain', that was also found in the P2X3R (Mansoor et al., 2016).
evidence: This refers to structural features identified in previous studies.

claim: In the P2X7R, the cap is stabilized by a highly palmitoylated membrane-associated Cys-anchor domain, which prevents desensitization.
source: In the P2X7R, however, this 'cap' is stabilized by a highly palmitoylated membrane-associated 'Cys-anchor' domain, which prevents desensitization.
evidence: This refers to structural features identified in cryo-EM studies.

claim: A stretch of 27–29 aa (S443-R471) was not resolved in the cryo-EM structure.
source: A stretch of 27–29 aa (S443-R471) was not resolved, and it is unclear if each ballast domain is formed by a single subunit or if a domain swap occurs between subunits (McCarthy et al., 2019).
evidence: This refers to limitations in the cryo-EM structural data.

claim: It is unclear if each ballast domain is formed by a single subunit or if a domain swap occurs between subunits.
source: A stretch of 27–29 aa (S443-R471) was not resolved, and it is unclear if each ballast domain is formed by a single subunit or if a domain swap occurs between subunits (McCarthy et al., 2019).
evidence: This refers to uncertainties in the structural interpretation.

claim: The molecular function of the ballast domain and how it is affected by ATP binding remain unclear.
source: While these structures represent a milestone in P2X7 research, the transition dynamics between receptor states in a cellular environment as well as the molecular function of the ballast domain and how it is affected by ATP binding remain unclear.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: The molecular mechanism of current facilitation is not understood.
source: Likewise, the molecular mechanism of current facilitation, a P2X7-characteristic process that describes faster and/or increased current responses upon repeated ATP application, is not understood.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Current facilitation is a P2X7-characteristic process that describes faster and/or increased current responses upon repeated ATP application.
source: Likewise, the molecular mechanism of current facilitation, a P2X7-characteristic process that describes faster and/or increased current responses upon repeated ATP application, is not understood.
evidence: This is a definition of current facilitation in the context of P2X7.

claim: Co-injection of mutated X. laevis eRF1(E55D) cRNA resulted in a more than threefold higher ratio of full-length and truncated receptor constructs compared to the 1-step injection method without eRF1(E55D).
source: Indeed, co-injection of either purified X. laevis eRF1(E55D) protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) or the respective in vitro synthesized cRNA (Figure 1C and D) resulted in a more than threefold higher ratio of full-length and truncated receptor constructs compared to the 1-step injection method without eRF1(E55D) and a smaller standard deviation compared to the 2-step injection method (1-step+eRF1(E55D): 1.469±0.229; 1-step: 0.418±0.082; 2-step: 1.603±0.933; mean ± S.D.).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the optimization experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: The optimized protocol led to more reproducible expression and increased formation of full-length ANAP-labeled receptors.
source: In conclusion, this optimized protocol led to more reproducible expression and increased formation of full-length ANAP-labeled receptors and was used in all following experiments.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the optimization experiments.

claim: All constructs with ANAP substitutions in the N-terminus and the head domain were formed in full length.
source: As shown in Figure 2C, all constructs with ANAP substitutions in the N-terminus and the head domain as well as three out of four constructs with substitutions in TM2 were formed in full length, indicating that receptors that are truncated before or within TM2 are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and likely undergo degradation.
evidence: This is a finding from the surface expression analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Three out of four constructs with ANAP substitutions in TM2 were formed in full length.
source: As shown in Figure 2C, all constructs with ANAP substitutions in the N-terminus and the head domain as well as three out of four constructs with substitutions in TM2 were formed in full length, indicating that receptors that are truncated before or within TM2 are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and likely undergo degradation.
evidence: This is a finding from the surface expression analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Receptors that are truncated before or within TM2 are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and likely undergo degradation.
source: As shown in Figure 2C, all constructs with ANAP substitutions in the N-terminus and the head domain as well as three out of four constructs with substitutions in TM2 were formed in full length, indicating that receptors that are truncated before or within TM2 are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum and likely undergo degradation.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that truncated receptors do not reach the surface.

claim: ANAP incorporation into G338 completely prevented membrane incorporation.
source: Interestingly, ANAP incorporation into G338 completely prevented membrane incorporation while cysteine substitution in the equivalent position of human P2X7R led previously to surface-expressed, but non-functional receptors (Pippel et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding from the surface expression analysis.

claim: Cysteine substitution in the equivalent position of human P2X7R (G338) led previously to surface-expressed, but non-functional receptors.
source: Interestingly, ANAP incorporation into G338 completely prevented membrane incorporation while cysteine substitution in the equivalent position of human P2X7R led previously to surface-expressed, but non-functional receptors (Pippel et al., 2017).
evidence: This refers to previous findings from another study.

claim: Surface expression of full-length receptors was particularly low for constructs containing ANAP in the C-terminal cap (K387*, C388*) and ballast (I577*) domains.
source: Surface expression of full-length receptors was particularly low for constructs containing ANAP in the C-terminal cap (K387*, C388*) and ballast (I577*) domains, while it was most efficient for ANAP-substitutions in positions 517–537 (in particular L527* and E537*) and in the very C-terminus (Y595* and 596*).
evidence: This is a finding from the surface expression analysis.

claim: Surface expression was most efficient for ANAP-substitutions in positions 517–537 (in particular L527* and E537*) and in the very C-terminus (Y595* and 596*).
source: Surface expression of full-length receptors was particularly low for constructs containing ANAP in the C-terminal cap (K387*, C388*) and ballast (I577*) domains, while it was most efficient for ANAP-substitutions in positions 517–537 (in particular L527* and E537*) and in the very C-terminus (Y595* and 596*).
evidence: This is a finding from the surface expression analysis.

claim: Most substitutions within the C-terminus led to a dominant formation of truncated P2X7 protein besides full-length receptors.
source: In summary, most substitutions within the C-terminus led to a dominant formation of truncated P2X7 protein besides full-length receptors.
evidence: This is a summary finding from the surface expression analysis.

claim: The majority of C-terminal constructs showed clear current responses.
source: Nevertheless, the majority of these constructs showed clear current responses (Figure 2C, Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the functional analysis shown in Figure 2C and Table 1.

claim: Control oocytes expressing wt P2X7R showed a gradual fluorescence decrease during ATP application, even when no ANAP was injected.
source: Control oocytes expressing wt P2X7R showed a gradual fluorescence decrease during ATP application, even when no ANAP was injected (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from control experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A similar fluorescence drift was observed with the P2X2R, but not with the hɑ1 GlyR or the fast-desensitizing P2X1R.
source: A similar fluorescence drift was observed with the P2X2R, but not with the hɑ1 GlyR or the fast-desensitizing P2X1R.
evidence: This is an observation from control experiments.

claim: All mutants in the head domain except E121* and Q128* showed clear fluorescence signals in all spectral segments.
source: In agreement with the pronounced conformational changes and ligand interactions of this domain during receptor activation (Lörinczi et al., 2012; McCarthy et al., 2019), all mutants except E121* and Q128* showed clear fluorescence signals in all spectral segments (Figure 3C and D, Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: For E121* and Q128* fluorescence changes were only detected with filter set 2.
source: For E121* and Q128* fluorescence changes were only detected with filter set 2, albeit with minimal changes for E121*.
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments.

claim: Fluorescence changes were always positive for P120* and G126* and negative for Y122*, P123*, and K127* independently of the wavelength.
source: Independently of the wavelength, fluorescence changes were always positive for P120* and G126* and negative for Y122*, P123*, and K127*.
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments.

claim: Consistent fluorescence changes over the entire ANAP emission spectrum indicate de-/quenching of ANAP either by the ligand ATP and/or other amino acid residues.
source: These consistent changes over the entire ANAP emission spectrum indicate de-/quenching of ANAP either by the ligand ATP and/or other aa residues (see insert table in Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fluorescence data.

claim: S124*, R125*, and Q128* showed positive fluorescence changes in most spectral segments but negative changes for wavelengths >500 nm.
source: In contrast, S124* (Figure 3E), R125*, and Q128* (Figure 3C and D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) showed positive fluorescence changes in most spectral segments but negative changes for wavelengths >500 nm.
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: The opposite directions of fluorescence changes in S124*, R125*, and Q128* imply that these changes result, at least partly, from an ANAP emission shift toward shorter wavelengths.
source: The opposite directions imply that these changes result, at least partly, from an ANAP emission shift toward shorter wavelengths and suggest that ANAP enters a less polar environment during receptor activation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fluorescence data.

claim: ANAP enters a less polar environment during receptor activation in positions S124*, R125*, and Q128*.
source: The opposite directions imply that these changes result, at least partly, from an ANAP emission shift toward shorter wavelengths and suggest that ANAP enters a less polar environment during receptor activation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fluorescence data based on ANAP photophysical properties.

claim: In all head-domain constructs that showed clear kinetics, with the exception of K127*, fluorescence and current changes started simultaneously and showed shorter rising times upon repeated ATP applications.
source: In all head-domain constructs that showed clear kinetics, with the exception of K127*, fluorescence and current changes started simultaneously and showed shorter rising times upon repeated ATP applications, thus recapitulating the characteristic 'current facilitation' of the P2X7R (Allsopp and Evans, 2015; Janks et al., 2019; Roger et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments.

claim: The S23N mutation did not eliminate current facilitation in rat P2X7, contrary to findings in human P2X7.
source: Contrary to findings in human P2X7 (Allsopp and Evans, 2015), the S23N mutation did not eliminate current facilitation in rat P2X7 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the functional analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Current rise times of the ΔCys mutant were not significantly altered between first and second ATP applications.
source: As expected (Roger et al., 2010) and in contrast to the wt and most of the analyzed ANAP-containing mutants, current rise times of the ΔCys mutant were not significantly altered between first and second ATP applications, demonstrating that we can indeed identify current facilitation in our setup (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the functional analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The K127* mutant showed a fluorescence change that was faster than the current increase already upon the first receptor activation.
source: Remarkably, the K127* mutant showed a fluorescence change that was faster than the current increase already upon the first receptor activation (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 3F.

claim: EC50 values for ATP were similar at wt, S124* and K127* mutants.
source: EC50 values for ATP were similar at wt, S124* and K127* mutants (Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the dose-response analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: ANAP in position 127 reports a process that precedes channel opening and is most likely related to ligand binding.
source: We conclude from this, that ANAP in position 127 reports a process that precedes channel opening and is most likely related to ligand binding, whereas ANAP reports gating-associated conformational changes in the other positions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic analysis of K127*.

claim: ANAP reports gating-associated conformational changes in head domain positions other than K127.
source: We conclude from this, that ANAP in position 127 reports a process that precedes channel opening and is most likely related to ligand binding, whereas ANAP reports gating-associated conformational changes in the other positions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the kinetic analysis.

claim: Current recordings from mutants S339*, T340*, and L341* were compromised by 10–20-fold higher leak currents compared to wt receptors or other mutants.
source: In agreement with a critical role in gating, current recordings from mutants S339*, T340*, and L341* were compromised by 10–20-fold higher leak currents compared to wt receptors or other mutants (see also Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the functional analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: P2X7R mutants S339* and L341* showed positive fluorescence signals in all spectral ranges.
source: While P2X7R mutants S339* and L341* showed positive signals in all spectral ranges, fluorescence changes in T340* were inconsistent at shorter emission wavelengths, but mostly negative below 470 nm, and positive above 470 nm, indicating again that a spectral shift contributed to these signals (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Fluorescence changes in T340* were inconsistent at shorter emission wavelengths, but mostly negative below 470 nm, and positive above 470 nm.
source: While P2X7R mutants S339* and L341* showed positive signals in all spectral ranges, fluorescence changes in T340* were inconsistent at shorter emission wavelengths, but mostly negative below 470 nm, and positive above 470 nm, indicating again that a spectral shift contributed to these signals (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: A spectral shift contributed to the fluorescence signals in T340*.
source: While P2X7R mutants S339* and L341* showed positive signals in all spectral ranges, fluorescence changes in T340* were inconsistent at shorter emission wavelengths, but mostly negative below 470 nm, and positive above 470 nm, indicating again that a spectral shift contributed to these signals (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the fluorescence data.

claim: Fluorescence signals from P2X7 T340* were significantly larger during the first ATP application compared to the second.
source: Notably, fluorescence signals from P2X7 T340* were also significantly larger during the first ATP application compared to the second (Figure 4B and C), suggesting that the environment of this position changed between both ATP applications.
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: The environment of position T340 changed between the first and second ATP applications.
source: Notably, fluorescence signals from P2X7 T340* were also significantly larger during the first ATP application compared to the second (Figure 4B and C), suggesting that the environment of this position changed between both ATP applications.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed difference in fluorescence amplitude.

claim: The T340* mutant displayed no change in fluorescence or current kinetics between ATP applications.
source: However, as the T340* mutant displayed no change in fluorescence or current kinetics between ATP applications (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1) the facilitation-associated gating mechanism is likely disturbed by this mutation.
evidence: This is a finding from the kinetic analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The facilitation-associated gating mechanism is likely disturbed by the T340* mutation.
source: However, as the T340* mutant displayed no change in fluorescence or current kinetics between ATP applications (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1) the facilitation-associated gating mechanism is likely disturbed by this mutation.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed lack of facilitation in T340*.

claim: All receptors with N-terminal ANAP substitutions were formed in full length.
source: Although all receptors with N-terminal ANAP substitutions were formed in full length (Figure 2C), current and fluorescence responses for S6*, V10*, and K17* substitutions remained small and inconsistent even after 6 days of expression.
evidence: This is a finding from the surface expression analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Current and fluorescence responses for S6*, V10*, and K17* substitutions remained small and inconsistent even after 6 days of expression.
source: Although all receptors with N-terminal ANAP substitutions were formed in full length (Figure 2C), current and fluorescence responses for S6*, V10*, and K17* substitutions remained small and inconsistent even after 6 days of expression.
evidence: This is a finding from the functional analysis.

claim: A3*, C5*, W7*, and F11* mutants showed positive fluorescence signals of variable sizes.
source: A3*, C5*, W7*, and F11* mutants showed positive fluorescence signals of variable sizes (Figure 5B), and the kinetics of F11* fluorescence correlated with current facilitation (Figure 5C, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The kinetics of F11* fluorescence correlated with current facilitation.
source: A3*, C5*, W7*, and F11* mutants showed positive fluorescence signals of variable sizes (Figure 5B), and the kinetics of F11* fluorescence correlated with current facilitation (Figure 5C, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: ANAP fluorescence in F11* was not quenched by the nearby Trp (W7).
source: ANAP fluorescence in F11* was not quenched by the nearby Trp (W7), as its removal had no apparent effect (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from control experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Surface expression of functional full-length receptors was observed for all C-terminal juxtamembrane constructs except for K387* and C388*.
source: Surface expression of functional full-length receptors was observed for all constructs except for K387* and C388*.
evidence: This is a finding from the surface expression analysis.

claim: Only one C-terminal juxtamembrane mutant, T361*, showed a fluorescence change, albeit in only ~50% of the recordings.
source: In contrast to the juxtamembrane N-terminal residues, however, only one of these C-terminal mutants, T361*, showed a fluorescence change, albeit in only ~50% of the recordings (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Both F11 and T361 lie within two of at least four possible cholesterol recognition amino acid consensus (CRAC) motifs.
source: Interestingly, both F11 and T361 lie within two of at least four possible cholesterol recognition amino acid consensus (CRAC) motifs that have been proposed to be involved in the cholesterol sensitivity of P2X7 channel gating (Robinson et al., 2014).
evidence: This refers to previous structural and functional studies.

claim: CRAC motifs have been proposed to be involved in the cholesterol sensitivity of P2X7 channel gating.
source: Interestingly, both F11 and T361 lie within two of at least four possible cholesterol recognition amino acid consensus (CRAC) motifs that have been proposed to be involved in the cholesterol sensitivity of P2X7 channel gating (Robinson et al., 2014).
evidence: This refers to previous studies on P2X7 regulation.

claim: ANAP introduction in most of the 29 ballast domain positions led to a dominant formation of truncated protein.
source: ANAP introduction in most of the 29 ballast domain positions led to a dominant formation of truncated protein, indicating that this domain does not tolerate substitutions very well and/or that the truncated constructs form stable proteins.
evidence: This is a finding from the surface expression analysis.

claim: The ballast domain does not tolerate substitutions very well and/or the truncated constructs form stable proteins.
source: ANAP introduction in most of the 29 ballast domain positions led to a dominant formation of truncated protein, indicating that this domain does not tolerate substitutions very well and/or that the truncated constructs form stable proteins.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of truncated protein formation.

claim: Four ballast domain mutants (Q422*, V424*, G538*, I577*) did not form functional receptors at all.
source: Four of these mutants (Q422*, V424*, G538*, I577*) did not form functional receptors at all.
evidence: This is a finding from the functional analysis.

claim: For most ballast domain constructs, no specific fluorescence changes could be detected, despite promising surface transport and current responses comparable to wt receptors for at least 12 of them.
source: For most of the remaining constructs, no specific fluorescence changes could be detected, despite promising surface transport and current responses comparable to wt receptors for at least 12 of them (see Table 1, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments summarized in Table 1.

claim: Only in two ballast domain mutants, A564* and D423*, fluorescence changes could be recorded.
source: Only in two mutants, A564* and D423*, fluorescence changes could be recorded: A564* showed clearly positive signals, while D423* showed positive signals in only ~40% of the recordings (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 5D.

claim: A564* showed clearly positive fluorescence signals.
source: Only in two mutants, A564* and D423*, fluorescence changes could be recorded: A564* showed clearly positive signals, while D423* showed positive signals in only ~40% of the recordings (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 5D.

claim: D423* showed positive signals in only ~40% of the recordings.
source: Only in two mutants, A564* and D423*, fluorescence changes could be recorded: A564* showed clearly positive signals, while D423* showed positive signals in only ~40% of the recordings (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from the VCF experiments shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Both A564* and D423* mutants showed EC50 values similar to wt P2X7.
source: Both mutants showed EC50 values similar to wt P2X7 and were not functional in control oocytes injected without ANAP (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the respective truncated proteins (compare Figure 2C) do either not contribute to current responses or only in complex with full-length (ANAP-containing) P2X7 subunits.
evidence: This is a finding from the dose-response analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: A564* and D423* were not functional in control oocytes injected without ANAP.
source: Both mutants showed EC50 values similar to wt P2X7 and were not functional in control oocytes injected without ANAP (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the respective truncated proteins (compare Figure 2C) do either not contribute to current responses or only in complex with full-length (ANAP-containing) P2X7 subunits.
evidence: This is a finding from control experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The truncated proteins from A564* and D423* constructs do either not contribute to current responses or only in complex with full-length (ANAP-containing) P2X7 subunits.
source: Both mutants showed EC50 values similar to wt P2X7 and were not functional in control oocytes injected without ANAP (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the respective truncated proteins (compare Figure 2C) do either not contribute to current responses or only in complex with full-length (ANAP-containing) P2X7 subunits.
evidence: This is an inference from the functional analysis.

claim: D423 is located within a loop connecting the β17 and β18 strands and situated on the outer surface of the cytoplasmic ballast, facing away from both the central axis of the receptor and the neighboring subunits.
source: D423 is located within a loop connecting the β17 and β18 strands and situated on the outer surface of the cytoplasmic ballast, facing away from both the central axis of the receptor and the neighboring subunits (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a structural description based on the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 5F.
